calls.head: Point-blank against perimeter
calls.body: On shot quality, Montréal sits 1st of 32, at the point-blank end of the scale. Nashville is 23rd, at the perimeter end.

calls.head: Nashville plays fast; Montréal slows it down
calls.body: Nashville ranks 5th of 32 for pace, toward the fast end; Montréal ranks 24th, toward the slow end.

surprises.head: Nashville won without the better chances
surprises.body: Expected goals favoured Montréal, 3.5 to 1.9, with empty nets left out. J. Saros stopped 1.5 more goals than expected.

surprises.head: Nashville shot far less than usual
surprises.body: 38.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5, adjusted for score and venue, against its usual 51.5.

surprises.head: Montréal shot far more than usual
surprises.body: 73.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5, adjusted for score and venue, against its usual 55.7.

surprises.head: Nashville tried a different line
surprises.body: A. Edstrom, J. Drury, R. Colton played 5:27 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Nashville’s usual lines.
